mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved monotonically from -30.1% to -18.6% over four weeks, signaling sustained recovery momentum. This trend continuation will drive RETAIL_REC further positive over the next four weeks as confidence in reopening solidifies.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 11.5 percentage points over t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or reverses by more than 5 percentage points in any single week.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has risen from -0.4% to +5.1% over four weeks, indicating restored confidence in essential-goods shopping. This behavioral shift reduces fear-driven avoidance and spills over to discretionary RETAIL_REC visits within the same shopping trips.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose 5.5 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below +2.0% in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to baseline within 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has declined from -35.0% to -25.1% over four weeks but remains severely depressed. If TRANSIT falls below -30.0% in the next week, it signals renewed restrictions that will suppress RETAIL_REC mobility through reduced foot traffic and consumer caution.
failure_condition: TRANSIT remains above -30.0% for all four weeks ahead, and RETAIL_REC continues to improve.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved from -22.1% to -12.0% over four weeks, indicating partial return to office work. This recovery in commuting patterns will drive weekday RETAIL_REC through increased lunchtime and after-work shopping, producing net positive RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by more than 2.0 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 10.1 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES declines in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its current level by week 2.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has deteriorated from -14.7% to -21.7% week-on-week, signaling reduced outdoor activity confidence. Combined with RESIDENTIAL remaining elevated at +16.0%, this indicates consumers are retreating indoors, suppressing both outdoor and retail mobility. RETAIL_REC will decline as outdoor-activity substitution effects reverse.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -20.0% and RESIDENTIAL remains above +15.0%
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined 8.3 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS recovers above -15.0% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC improves despite the PARKS-RESIDENTIAL interaction.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility jointly signal policy regime. When both remain depressed (TRANSIT < -25%, WORKPLACES < -15%), it indicates ongoing restrictions. Under this regime, RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed as consumer mobility is constrained by policy, not preference.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -25.0% AND WORKPLACES remains below -15.0%
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -25.1% and WORKPLACES at -12.0% in t-0w
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES improves by more than 5 percentage points in any single week, or RETAIL_REC exceeds -10.0% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-July in Singapore typically marks school holiday season and peak summer leisure demand. PARKS decline (-21.7%) suggests outdoor venues are capacity-constrained or closed. Consumers will redirect leisure spending to indoor retail venues, driving RETAIL_REC recovery despite PARKS weakness.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -15.0% during school holiday window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within two weeks, or PARKS recovers above -10.0% while RETAIL_REC remains flat.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stabilized at +5.1% while RETAIL_REC remains at -18.6%, indicating a bifurcation: essential shopping has recovered but discretionary spending has not. If GROCERY_PHARM continues to improve, it signals consumer confidence recovery that will eventually spill into RETAIL_REC as fear-driven avoidance diminishes.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM sustains above +4.0% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved 5.5 points over four weeks while RETAIL_REC improved only 11.5 points
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below +2.0% in any of the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not improve by at least 3 percentage points by week 4.
